prompt: How do I create a combo chart in Excel?
completion:
### How to Create a Combo Chart in Excel  
A **combo chart** lets you display two (or more) data series with different chart types on the same graph—e.g., a column chart for sales and a line chart for profit margin.  
Below are the most common steps for Excel 2016‑2023 (the steps are very similar in 2013 and 2010, with minor UI differences).  

---

## 1. Prepare Your Data  

| **Month** | **Revenue** | **Profit %** |
|-----------|-------------|--------------|
| Jan       | 120,000     | 12%          |
| Feb       | 145,000     | 15%          |
| Mar       | 130,000     | 10%          |
| …         | …           | …            |

- **Column 1**: Category (e.g., month, product).  
- **Column 2**: First series you want as columns (Revenue).  
- **Column 3**: Second series you want as a line (Profit %).  

> **Tip**: Keep the category column on the left; it will be used as the X‑axis for the chart.

---

## 2. Insert a Combo Chart

### a. Select the Data
Click and drag to highlight the entire table **including headers** (e.g., A1:C4).

### b. Insert the Chart
1. **Home** ► **Clipboard** ► **Copy** (optional)  
2. Go to the **Insert** tab.  
3. In the **Charts** group, click the small arrow beneath **Recommended Charts**.  
4. Choose **All Charts** tab.  
5. Select **Combo** from the left‑hand list.

### c. Pick a Pre‑Set Combo or Build Custom
- **Recommended combo**: Excel will suggest a combo that matches your data.  
- **Custom**: You can define which series uses which chart type.

For a custom combo:
1. Click **Custom** (or the “Custom combo” button).
2. For each series, pick a chart type:
   - **Revenue** → Column (or Bar).
   - **Profit %** → Line (or Scatter).
3. Check “Plot series on secondary axis” **only** for the series that has a different scale (e.g., percentages vs. dollars).  
4. Click **OK**.

---

## 3. Fine‑Tune the Chart

### a. Format Series
- **Right‑click** the series on the chart → **Format Data Series**.  
- For the line series:
  - Set **Marker** options (size, shape).  
  - Change **Line style** (solid, dashed).  
  - Optionally add **Data labels**.

### b. Add Secondary Axis (if needed)
If the two series are on different scales (e.g., $ vs. %), Excel may automatically add a secondary Y‑axis.  
- **Right‑click** the series → **Format Data Series** → **Series Options** → **Plot Series on Secondary Axis**.  

### c. Adjust Axes
- Click on an axis → **Format Axis**.  
  - Set **Minimum / Maximum** bounds.  
  - Format numbers (currency, percent).  
  - Change tick marks, gridlines.

### d. Chart Title & Legend
- Click the chart title → edit text.  
- Click the legend → reposition, edit series names.

### e. Data Table / Gridlines
Add a data table by **Chart Elements** (green plus sign) → **Data Table**.  
Toggle major/minor gridlines the same way.

---

## 4. Save & Reuse the Chart

- **Copy** the chart → Paste into PowerPoint, Word, or another workbook.  
- To make a **template**:  
  1. Select the chart.  
  2. Right‑click → **Save as Template…**.  
  3. Name it (e.g., “Sales‑Profit Combo”).  
  Next time, you can insert it via **Insert** ► **Recommended Charts** ► **Templates**.

---

## 5. Quick Cheat‑Sheet (for Excel 2016+)

| Action | Shortcut |
|--------|----------|
| Insert Combo Chart | **Insert** ► **Recommended Charts** ► **All Charts** ► **Combo** |
| Format series | Right‑click series ► **Format Data Series** |
| Add secondary axis | Format series ► **Series Options** ► **Secondary Axis** |
| Change chart type for a series | Right‑click series ► **Change Series Chart Type** |
| Show/hide gridlines | **Chart Elements** ► **Gridlines** |
| Add data labels | **Chart Elements** ► **Data Labels** |
| Add data table | **Chart Elements** ► **Data Table** |

---

### Common Pitfalls & Fixes

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| Secondary axis appears for both series | Make sure you only check **Plot series on secondary axis** for the series that needs it. |
| Line appears inside the bars, not over them | Set the line series to **Plot series on secondary axis** or change the **Series order** (right‑click → **Bring to Front**). |
| Percent values show as 0.12 instead of 12% | Format the Y‑axis → **Number** → **Percentage**. |
| Axis titles missing | **Chart Elements** ► **Axis Titles** ► **Primary Vertical** / **Secondary Vertical** |

---

## 6. Excel 2010/2007 Tips

- In **2010**, the combo option is under **Insert** ► **Charts** ► **Combo** (bottom of the dialog).  
- In **2007**, click **Insert** ► **Chart** → choose **Line** → then right‑click the chart → **Change Chart Type** → pick **Combo**.

---

## 7. Example: Sales vs. Profit Margin (Combo)

1. **Insert → Combo → Custom**.  
2. Set **Revenue** → **Clustered Column**.  
3. Set **Profit %** → **Line** (secondary axis).  
4. Right‑click **Profit %** → **Add Data Labels** → format as percentages.  
5. Title: “Monthly Sales & Profit Margin”  
6. Adjust Y‑axes: Primary → Currency, Secondary → Percentage.

---

### Final Checklist

- [ ] Data organized (categories + series)  
- [ ] Chart inserted as **Combo**  
- [ ] Correct chart types chosen for each series  
- [ ] Secondary axis set where needed  
- [ ] Axes formatted properly (scale, number format)  
- [ ] Titles, legend, and data labels added  
- [ ] Chart saved as a template (optional)

That’s it! You now have a professional‑looking combo chart that lets viewers see two related metrics side by side. Happy charting!
